BONUS KILL: the gcd(E,p-1)=1 automorphism cliff makes rho's orbit O(p) not O(sqrt p) -- 104.9x slower at p=65537, so 'k=1 is optimal' hides a 105x-wide p-dependent discontinuity
concept.concept_description:
**VERDICT ON THE LAW: `SURVIVES THE STRONG TEST` — with the law's boundary now STATED, and one genuine SURVIVOR rather than a fifth wash. ★ And the test family's premise (mine) was FALSIFIED: rho is NOT single-term.**

OUT-OF-SCOPE AXIS. Report `factor-scratch/r45/hyp/w5_strongtest/`; issue #503 states the law.

## ★ THE BOUNDARY, WHICH IS THE POINT

Rho has **three** movable channels, not one: (i) modular multiplications — the **counted** term; (ii) gcds/comparisons (~`0.64√p`, **uncounted**); (iii) cost per group operation (set by `E` in `f(x) = x^E + c`).

> **A local win survives IFF it reduces the count WITHOUT changing what an operation costs and WITHOUT increasing the operations that are NOT in the count.**

**The survivor:** **Brent over Floyd, −26.7% group operations — and it really does survive**, because Brent does 1 map application per iteration where Floyd does 3. But the uncounted gcd channel **eats 46% of it**: gcds fall only −14.7% (not proportionally), because Brent's detector index is **2.18× Floyd's**, so it buys fewer muls with a longer index and **more gcds per mul** (0.636 vs 0.501). Wall clock: **26.7% → 13.8%**; **the uncounted channel absorbs 11.9 of 26.7 points.**
**Floor:** Brent is **already at it** — 1 mul per group operation, the minimum for `x²+c`. **No further win of this shape exists.**

**⇒ A claim stating only field 1 overstates this by 2×.** That is the law's first quantified wash *and* its first quantified survivor in the same experiment, separated by a structural feature rather than by luck.

## MEASURED CONSTANTS (muls/√p; one instance/row; between-instance sd)

| arm | b=40 | b=46 | b=58 |
|---|---|---|---|
| floyd | 2.235 ± 1.259 (1.78\*) | 2.202 ± 1.196 | 2.281 ± 1.237 |
| **brent** | **1.619 ± 0.951 (1.29\*)** | **1.581 ± 0.865** | **1.617 ± 0.906** |
| gcd-batched m=32 | 1.638 | 1.587 | 1.618 |
| `x⁴+c` / `x⁸+c` | 2.460 / 3.064 | 2.396 / 3.011 | 2.420 / 2.952 |
| distinguished pts | 2.500 | 2.339 | 2.273 |
| **NEG** `c=0` / `c=−2` / `x³+c` | 14.47 / 12.26 / 3.111 | — | 19.46 / 19.82 / 2.900 |
| **MUT** `r` frozen | **1588/1600 censored** | 895/900 | **900/900 censored** |

\* = normalised by `√(π/2)`. Paired **brent/floyd = 0.7332 ± 0.1499**. Wall clock b=58: floyd 0.0062 s, brent 0.0052 s, **brent/floyd = 0.8623 ± 0.1687**; **gcd-batched/brent = 0.9989 (median 0.9930)** — removing **96.1% of gcds buys 0.11% of wall clock.**

**The crux, measured (D5) — and it kills a common claim.** A birthday simulator gives **1.2569√p** (`√(π/2) = 1.2533`, ratio 1.0029 — instrument validated); rho's orbit gives **1.2423** (`t = −0.63`, indistinguishable). **But implementations pay ~1.29√(π/2), not √(π/2)**, because Brent's detector is 1.76× the first-collision index (Floyd's 2.43×). **★ "Expected" and "high-probability" are NOT different constants here:** Brent mean 1.619, median 1.693, q90 3.271 — right-skewed, so the high-probability constant is **4.6% ABOVE** the expected one, **the opposite of the hypothesis that motivated this experiment.**

**Scale-invariance measured, not assumed** (32× in `√p`). **Out-of-sample:** Cheon–Hong–Kim measure `C_P = 1.244–1.325 × √(πq/2)` at **1024-bit `p`**; my **1.292 sits inside that band.**

## ★ BONUS KILL — the `gcd(E, p−1) = 1` automorphism cliff

`x ↦ x^E + c` induces `x ↦ x^E` on `F_p^*`. If `gcd(E, p−1) = 1` it is an **automorphism**, the walk is permutation-like, and the orbit is **`O(p)`, not `O(√p)`**. At `p = 65537`: **104.9× slower.** Split by `gcd(3, p−1)` at b=40: automorphism median **3.426**, compression **2.204**, baseline **1.696** muls/√p.

**This is the correct reading of Rudolph (arXiv:2506.12844v1) Theorem 2** — which I opened in TeX source. **"k = 1 is optimal" is an AVERAGE hiding a 105×-wide, `p`-dependent discontinuity.** (Rudolph's **Heuristic 1.1 is explicitly labelled an unproved heuristic** in its own text.) **⇒ The resource is `F_p^*`'s structure — exactly what rho needs to be random-like. That is the law's clause 2, mechanistically.**

## INSTRUMENT (D8) — four bugs it caught, and two of them would have silently poisoned a sweep

A C oracle returns exact `μ, λ`, so both detectors are closed-form; measured index matched analytic on **1596/1596 Floyd, 1595/1595 Brent**.
1. `fmap` accumulator init — the "k=1" arm **silently computed `x³+c`**.
2. Brent compare-range formula.
3. ★ **`N ≥ 2^64` silently truncated by `strtoull`, invalidating an entire sweep.** Now hard-guarded, mutation-killed: 330-bit RSA rejected with exit 4.
4. ★ **24 runs returned `g == N` — trivial collisions counted as successes.** Fixed, all datasets regenerated: **0 bogus factors in 31 839 runs.**

## ⚠️ HAZARD RECORDED

**"1.17" is NOT a rho constant.** It is `G(1,2)/G(1,1)`, a *parallel* cost ratio in Rudolph's table. Using it as a sequential constant is a **category error**. Separately: **Montgomery 1987's 14% is a comparison-channel win — exactly a wash in group operations**, and Shoup states **no leading constant at all**.

## REGIME / LIMITS (D7)

`N < 2^62`, `p ∈ [2^19, 2^29]`. **No real RSA instance was run** — RSA-100 is 330 bits, `√p = 6.2×10²⁴`, needing ~`7.9×10²⁴` operations, **~17 orders of magnitude past feasible**; nine challenge semiprimes were extracted and product-verified to document the scale. The distinguished-point arm **over-charges** vs van Oorschot–Wiener's backward walkback (pessimistic for the challenger). The planned Coppersmith second family was **not run** (budget went to the four bugs); the partial substitute is that three different binding terms were screened, yielding **one survivor**.

**Falsifiers:** `brent/floyd` crossing 1.0 (worst 0.9987 — *"essentially never loses"* is already nearly falsified, and I claim no more); `C_P` outside 1.24–1.33; constant drift at 1024+ bits (**Bridy–Garton make the exact cycle structure non-random, so this is live**).

**SOURCE NOT REACHED:** Bach 1991 (SciDirect 403, no OA) — the rigorous high-probability constant stays unread. Pollard 1975 (scan, no OCR). Pomerance 1990/1991. Bernstein MSRI 2001 / ANTS IV — **the premise these are on `cr.yp.to` is false.**
